Definition: to fail; by implication to wear out, decay (causatively, consume, spend)
BiblicalUsage: Balah means to wear out, to grow old and fail. Moses tells Israel their clothes did not wear out in forty years of wilderness, Nehemiah says the same of their feet, Job says a man wastes away like a rotten thing, and Isaiah says the enemies of God's servant will wear out like a garment.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word draws the line between what God keeps and what time eats away. Clothes last forty years when God is keeping them, and the proud wear out like moth-eaten cloth when He is done with them.
